records.title: Relationship between onset of altitude-decompression disorders in man and barometric pressure level during intensive physical exercise
records.byline: Vakar MI, Mazin AN, Tsivilashvili AS, Malchikov VV

observations.protocol: No preliminary oxygen prebreathe. Oxygen from chamber ascent onward. Six-hour target protocol with 40 minutes work and 20 minutes rest per cycle. Work energy expenditure reported as 400–450 kcal/h by indirect calorimetry.
observations.outcome_window: The report describes continuous examination during the test and 24-hour hospitalization for affected volunteers. Fixed surveillance for event-free volunteers after descent is unspecified.
observations.note: Results give 0.4 atm and 308 mm Hg as ambient pressure. Methods p. 112 labels 0.3 atm as suit excess pressure. Both cases were mild. Printed 0.41% differs from 2/434 (0.46% when rounded to two decimals). NASA TM-76015 p. 6 (PDF p. 9) repeats 2/434 at 0.4 atm and prints 0.46%.

observations.protocol: No preliminary oxygen prebreathe. Oxygen from chamber ascent onward. Six-hour target protocol with 40 minutes work and 20 minutes rest per cycle. Work energy expenditure reported as 400–450 kcal/h by indirect calorimetry.
observations.outcome_window: The report describes continuous examination during the test and 24-hour hospitalization for affected volunteers. Fixed surveillance for event-free volunteers after descent is unspecified.
observations.note: Results give 0.35 atm ambient, and Methods use 0.35 atm as suit excess pressure. Exact mm Hg was not printed for this arm. Some symptoms were more marked. The report does not tabulate severity counts. NASA TM-76015 p. 6 (PDF p. 9) repeats the same arm count and pressure.

trial_scopes.note: Seventy men aged 20–40. Exposure-by-person linkage unavailable.
Counts refer to tests. Pressure is the printed ambient mm Hg in Results.
Ambient pressure of 0.35 atm as printed. No conversion of this source value to mm Hg.

records.title: Hypobaric nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere as a method for preventing high-altitude decompression disease
records.byline: Genin AM, Chernyakov IN, Maksimov IV, Glazkova VA

observations.protocol: A six- to eight-hour initial stage at 553 mm Hg with nominal 40% oxygen and 60% nitrogen in the Methods, followed by the 248 mm Hg final stage breathing pure oxygen. Six trials lasted two to three hours and 14 lasted five to six hours at the target.
observations.outcome_window: Symptoms during the reported final exposure. Fixed postdescent follow-up is unspecified.
observations.note: No HADD symptoms in 20 tests involving 16 people. Result spans JPRS pp. 73–74. The Methods give 248 mm Hg at the target and the conclusions use 250 mm Hg.

observations.protocol: Eight hours at the preliminary 2.6 km stage, with a nominal 40% oxygen and 60% nitrogen mixture, then pure oxygen during ascent and the nominal 180 mm Hg final chamber stage. Three-hour target exposure in the protocol.
observations.outcome_window: Symptoms during the reported final exposure. Fixed postdescent follow-up is unspecified.
observations.note: The Results identify 15 fully executed tests at 10.6 km without HADD symptoms. This is a completion subset within the 18-experiment series.

observations.protocol: Eight hours at 550 mm Hg breathing nominal 40% oxygen and 60% nitrogen, then three hours wearing a 180 mm Hg pressurized suit in a chamber at 2 mm Hg.
observations.outcome_window: Symptoms during the reported final exposure. Fixed postdescent follow-up is unspecified.
observations.note: The p. 75 methods identify two suited tests. P. 76 explicitly reports no HADD symptoms in the suited tests and summarizes 17 experiments. The individual crosswalk to the series is unavailable.

observations.protocol: Eight hours at the preliminary 2.6 km stage, with a nominal 40% oxygen and 60% nitrogen mixture, then pure oxygen during ascent and the nominal 180 mm Hg final chamber stage. Three-hour target exposure in the protocol.
observations.outcome_window: Began immediately on reaching the target in a selected altered trial.
observations.note: Poor tolerance resolved at higher pressure and recurred on re-ascent within the same experiment. The source identifies meteorism and describes a later repeat trial without it. The observation is one described episode, with no comparable risk set assigned.

trial_scopes.note: Two series. People participated in both, as indicated by the overlapping person margins. Individual crosswalk unavailable.
The Methods report target pressure 248 mm Hg. Conclusions describe approximately 250 mm Hg.
The source describes a second-series total and varying final exposure conditions.
Fifteen completed at the 10.6 km chamber target.
Pressure is inside the suit. Chamber ambient was 2 mm Hg. The p. 76 summary of 17 matches the 15 completed chamber tests and two suited tests. Primary text does not identify each test.

records.title: Effect exerted on the human and animal body by repeated exposure in a rarefied atmosphere
records.byline: Petrukhin VG, Terentyev VG, Chernyakov IN

observations.protocol: Repeated human chamber experiments at 11–12 km on oxygen after heterogeneous 20-minute to four-hour desaturation. Target time was typically two to three hours, ranging up to 24 hours in the longer tests.
observations.outcome_window: Examination before, during and after chamber ascent. Affected individuals were hospitalized as indicated. Fixed surveillance duration across the full series is unspecified.
observations.note: Ten experiments with minor functional findings such as fatigue, headache, tremor and autonomic changes. Source-defined neurological observation with heterogeneous clinical findings.

observations.protocol: Repeated human chamber experiments at 11–12 km on oxygen after heterogeneous 20-minute to four-hour desaturation. Target time was typically two to three hours, ranging up to 24 hours in the longer tests.
observations.outcome_window: Examination before, during and after chamber ascent. Affected individuals were hospitalized as indicated. Fixed surveillance duration across the full series is unspecified.
observations.note: Three distinct cases with more prominent complaints and neurological changes from the 133-experiment human series. Two narratives report acute decompression disease. The report cannot establish DCS as the cause in the third. No total acute DCS count was given.

observations.protocol: Repeated human chamber experiments at 11–12 km on oxygen after heterogeneous 20-minute to four-hour desaturation. Target time was typically two to three hours, ranging up to 24 hours in the longer tests.
observations.outcome_window: Selected case narrative at altitude and after descent.
observations.note: Chest pain noted in hour six at 12 km in the fifth test. Attribution of the neurological changes to decompression disease could not be established.

milestones.note: Reached in the sixth hour at 12 km. Exact onset minute unavailable.

observations.outcome_window: Selected case narrative at altitude and after descent.

observations.outcome_window: Selected case narrative at altitude and after descent.
observations.note: The authors identified right wrist pain followed by sternal pain at altitude as decompression disease. Exact altitude for this case is unspecified.
